instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Slice the baguette into 1/2-inch slices, brush both sides with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and spread them on a baking sheet. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until crisp and golden.

Meanwhile, make the rouille. Mince 2 of the garlic cloves with 1 roasted red pepper from the jar until it's a rough paste. Crumble 1 pinch of the saffron into 1 tsp warm water, then stir it into the mayonnaise with the pepper paste and the cayenne. That should be about 1/2 cup. Put it in a small bowl for the table.

Cut the fennel in half, slice the bulb thinly and keep the fronds. Slice the white and light green part of the leek into rings and rinse them. Slice the shallot. Cut the potatoes into 3/4-inch chunks.
Heat the remaining 3 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the fennel seeds and stir for 30 seconds, until they smell toasty.
Add the fennel, leek, shallot and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Mince the remaining 3 garlic cloves and add them. Stir for 30 seconds. Peel 3 long strips of zest off the orange.
Pour in the white wine and add the orange zest, the remaining pinch of saffron and the bay leaves. Bubble for 2 minutes, until it's reduced by about half.
Add the potatoes, the diced tomatoes with their juice and the fish stock. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides easily into a potato.
Cut the cod into 2-inch chunks and sprinkle them with 1/2 tsp of the salt. Scrub the clams.
Add the cod and clams, cover, and cook for 5 minutes. The cod is done when it flakes.
Add the shrimp, cover, and cook for 2 minutes, until they're pink and curled. Throw out any clams that stay shut.
Take out the orange zest and the bay leaves. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle it into bowls and scatter the fennel fronds over the top. Serve with the croutons and the rouille, spooning a little rouille onto each crouton.
method_notes: The lead (Tasting Table, 5 stars from 64 ratings) builds the broth from fennel, leek, saffron, orange zest and a potato base, adds the fish and clams last, and serves rouille alongside; Tyler Florence's (no rating shown) marinates the fish and uses a long fumet. I followed the lead's order but used bought fish stock and a mayonnaise rouille from Tyler Florence's version so it fits a weeknight, and left out the Pernod, using fennel seeds and white wine for the anise note. The Mediterranean Dish version blocked me, so it was not read.
